questions.prompt: The Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria were amalgamated in
questions.explanation: Lord Lugard oversaw the amalgamation of 1 January 1914. 1960 is the year of independence, the nearest confusion, but that is a different event.

questions.prompt: Which three ethnic groups are the largest in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Hausa-Fulani, Yoruba and Igbo together make up the largest shares of the population. Ijaw and Kanuri are major groups but smaller, which is why the first wrong option is tempting.

questions.prompt: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded after a jihad led by
questions.explanation: Usman dan Fodio began the Fulani jihad in 1804 and founded the Sokoto Caliphate. Mai Idris Alooma was a ruler of Kanem-Bornu centuries earlier, so he is the nearest wrong name.

questions.prompt: The Nok culture of central Nigeria is best known for

options.text: terracotta sculptures and early iron smelting

questions.explanation: Nok produced terracotta figures and is linked to early iron working in West Africa. Bronze plaques belong to Benin, which is why they are the nearest wrong answer.

questions.prompt: The traditional ruler of the Benin Kingdom is called the
questions.explanation: The ruler of Benin is the Oba. The Ooni rules Ife, and he is the nearest wrong choice because both are Southern titles that are easy to confuse.

questions.prompt: Nigeria attained independence from Britain on
questions.explanation: Independence was on 1 October 1960. 1 October 1963 is when Nigeria became a republic, the nearest wrong date, and that event changed the head of state rather than ending colonial rule.

questions.prompt: Nigeria's capital was officially moved from Lagos to Abuja in
questions.explanation: The move became official on 12 December 1991. The decision to create a new capital was announced in 1976, which is why 1976 is the nearest wrong choice: it marks the decision, not the move.

questions.prompt: Which statement about languages in Nigeria is correct?

options.text: Nigeria has fewer than ten languages and Hausa is the official language
Yoruba is the only language taught in all schools
Nigeria has several hundred languages, and English is the official language
English was replaced as the official language in 1960

questions.explanation: Linguists count about five hundred languages in Nigeria, and English is the official language used in government and education. Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo are major national languages, but none is the official language.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a reason Nigeria's cultural diversity is considered a national asset?

options.text: It guarantees that all citizens speak one language
It removes the need for a central government
It supplies a wide range of arts, food, music and trade networks
It prevents any group from migrating

questions.explanation: Diversity enriches the arts, cuisine, festivals and commerce. Saying it guarantees one language contradicts the meaning of diversity.

questions.prompt: Traditional marriage among most Nigerian peoples is best described as

options.text: a purely private contract with no family role
a union between two families as well as two individuals
a legal act that only a court can perform
a ceremony restricted to one ethnic group

questions.explanation: Across Nigerian cultures, marriage joins families and involves rites such as bride price or introductions. Treating it as a private contract misses the role of the extended family.
